candidates.catalyst: Direct sales and sales reorganization can retain channel economics and expand operating margins. Construction Cloud and design/manufacturing subscriptions can increase product attach and recurring revenue. MaintainX can add maintenance-software subscriptions and cross-selling, offset by integration costs. AI design/workflow features can support higher-value subscription tiers; incremental AI revenue is not separately verified.
candidates.risk: Construction/manufacturing budgets, MaintainX integration and cash-collection comparability; historical accounting-practices litigation warrants monitoring.
candidates.quality: Latest GAAP operating margin 29.3% versus 25.2%; gross margin 91.4% versus 91.0%. Latest net-income growth also benefits from a lower tax rate.
candidates.options: No live option-chain snapshot: liquidity, bid/ask spread, IV, delta and open interest remain unverified. No specific contract recommended. Research 18–30 month expirations when listed and ~0.70–0.85 delta ITM calls; verify break-even and avoid an IV spike.
candidates.down: Software valuation compression, AI disruption concerns, sales-channel changes and cash-flow guidance affected by MaintainX acquisition costs. The historical 2024 cash-flow-practices investigations closed in August 2025; shareholder litigation remains a governance risk.
candidates.cash: TTM FCF $2.84B, +50.7% YoY; latest quarter $561M, +24.4%. OCF $575M; capex $14M. Direct-sales transaction changes affect collection timing, so do not extrapolate one cash-rich quarter.
candidates.margins: Latest GAAP operating margin 29.3% versus 25.2%; gross margin 91.4% versus 91.0%. Latest net-income growth also benefits from a lower tax rate.
candidates.balance: About $4.16B cash/investments versus $3.71B total debt including leases (secondary aggregation). FY27 SBC guidance about 9% of revenue. Latest diluted shares 211M versus 215M a year earlier.
catalysts: Direct sales and sales reorganization can retain channel economics and expand operating margins.
Construction Cloud and design/manufacturing subscriptions can increase product attach and recurring revenue.
MaintainX can add maintenance-software subscriptions and cross-selling, offset by integration costs.
AI design/workflow features can support higher-value subscription tiers; incremental AI revenue is not separately verified.
candidates.moat: AutoCAD/Revit file formats, installed users and embedded design workflows produce substantial switching costs.
candidates.valuation: At about 17.0x TTM FCF / 30.0x GAAP earnings, attractive relative to 30.3x P/FCF at Q3 FY26 and 34.4x at Q2 FY26. Cheaper on cash flow than Reddit; it earns a premium over slower Accenture. Consensus forward P/E (~17.8x) may use adjusted EPS.
candidates.recovery: A return to the $344.39 August 2021 high is fundamentally plausible over 12–36 months if recurring growth and margin gains persist. That old valuation is not guaranteed.
candidates.invalidation: Organic growth slips to low single digits, GAAP operating margins reverse materially, cash collection worsens, or new material accounting findings emerge.

candidates.catalyst: Procedure growth, da Vinci 5 adoption, recurring instruments/accessories and service revenue, Ion expansion, international installed-base growth, and digital/AI-enabled surgical workflow improvements.
candidates.risk: Premium valuation, hospital capital budgets, procedure-growth deceleration, competition, manufacturing execution and regulatory/product-cycle risk.
candidates.quality: Q2 GAAP gross margin 67.8% versus 66.3% a year earlier; GAAP operating income rose to $971.9M from $743.4M while revenue grew 18.5%.
candidates.options: Delayed public chain references exist, but live delta, spread and IV must be rechecked before entry. Prefer 18–30 month expirations when available and roughly 0.70–0.85 delta ITM calls.
candidates.down: The stock experienced a major valuation reset from its 52-week high despite continued double-digit procedure, revenue and earnings growth. The setup is valuation compression plus a support/base test rather than a broken earnings story.
candidates.cash: Current secondary valuation data imply roughly $3.2B of TTM free cash flow. The company ended Q2 with $8.63B of cash, cash equivalents and investments and only $2.58B of total liabilities.
candidates.margins: Q2 GAAP gross margin 67.8% versus 66.3%; GAAP operating income $971.9M versus $743.4M. Revenue, operating profit and net income all increased YoY.
candidates.balance: $8.63B cash/investments against $2.58B total liabilities at Q2; shares outstanding have declined about 1.1% YoY in current secondary data.
catalysts: Worldwide da Vinci/Ion procedures continue compounding, increasing recurring instruments, accessories and service revenue.
da Vinci 5 adoption expands the installed base and can support higher utilization and recurring ecosystem revenue.
Ion procedure growth expands Intuitive beyond traditional surgery into minimally invasive lung diagnostics.
Digital workflow, analytics and AI-assisted capabilities can deepen hospital integration and switching costs.
candidates.moat: Large installed base, surgeon training, hospital workflow integration, regulatory experience, recurring instruments/accessories, service ecosystem and clinical adoption create substantial switching costs.
candidates.valuation: About 46.6x trailing GAAP earnings and 44.5x FCF remains a premium valuation, but it has compressed sharply from roughly 70x earnings and 80x FCF at FY2025. This is a quality-compounder valuation reset, not a cheap-stock setup.
candidates.recovery: A return toward the $603.88 52-week high is possible over a multi-year horizon if procedure growth, placements and earnings continue compounding, but the prior premium multiple should not be assumed.
candidates.invalidation: Procedure growth falls materially below the low-teens range, system placements weaken persistently, margins structurally deteriorate, competitive adoption accelerates against Intuitive, or valuation remains excessive relative to growth.
candidates.optionNote: Jan 2028 delayed chain shows usable ITM open interest at several strikes, but live delta, bid/ask spread and IV remain unverified. Do not treat delayed contract data as a standing order.
sectorLongTermGood: Aging populations and minimally invasive surgery support procedure growth
Installed systems drive recurring instruments, accessories and service revenue
Training and workflow integration create high switching costs
sectorLongTermRisk: Hospital capital budgets can delay system placements
Medical-device regulation and product-cycle execution matter
Competition could pressure system pricing or procedure share

candidates.risk: Dependence on search referrals, weaker US user growth, advertising budgets and data/privacy regulation.

candidates.down: High-growth valuation compression and concerns that search engines and AI summaries will divert traffic. The Q2 earnings selloff occurred despite revenue and profit growth; revenue growth slowed from about 69% to 61%.
candidates.cash: TTM FCF $1.02B, +156.7% YoY. Latest FCF $260.7M, +135.3%; OCF $261.9M. Latest FCF margin 32.4% versus 22.2%.
candidates.margins: Latest gross margin 91.3% versus 90.8%; operating margin 28.8% versus 13.5%. Revenue, operating profit, net income and cash flow improve together.

catalysts: AI-assisted Max ad campaigns and creative automation can improve advertiser conversion and ad pricing.
Shopify integration and performance ads can broaden paying advertisers and commerce ad spend.
International monetization: Q2 international revenue +84% and ARPU +31%; translation expands accessible audiences.
Data licensing can add high-margin revenue, but new large agreements are not assumed in the base case.
candidates.moat: Community network effects and a proprietary corpus of human conversations; advertising is recurring activity rather than contracted SaaS revenue.
candidates.valuation: 28.1x P/FCF and 34.7x GAAP P/E: attractive for sustained growth, but not conventionally cheap. P/FCF was about 84.5x at September 2025. More expensive than Adobe, Autodesk and Salesforce; requires much faster growth.
candidates.recovery: The $263.50 January 2026 high is plausibly recoverable if user monetization and cash growth continue; stronger direct/logged-in engagement would reduce the main risk.
candidates.invalidation: Persistent direct-user or engagement erosion, ad growth drops sharply without offsetting monetization, gross margins deteriorate, or data-access restrictions undermine the moat.

sourcesUsed: Massive historical daily prices and available legacy financial statements
Current SEC filings, company releases and web research
method: Two-lane profitable-company LEAPS universe. Lane A seeks deep 30–70% drawdowns; Lane B admits high-quality profitable compounders on smaller pullbacks or major support/valuation resets. GAAP profitability, revenue quality, cash generation, valuation, moat and thesis integrity remain strict. Tariff exposure is not a qualification filter or score penalty. Tariff headlines may explain a temporary dip but do not automatically exclude hardware or med-tech businesses. Option quality remains provisional until live delta, IV and spreads are verified. Sector and industry context is included for every qualified company with explicit long-term tailwinds and structural risks. Fundamental expiration targets now use a Bear/Base/Bull blended GAAP P/E + P/FCF model tied to Jan 2029. Contract selection must be tested against these targets rather than prior highs alone.

hardGates: Positive TTM free cash flow or clearly strong operating cash generation
No going-concern/accounting crisis or structurally broken core business
qualificationModel.laneA: Deep Discount / Recovery: usually 30–70% below a meaningful high.
qualificationModel.laneB: Quality Compounder Pullback: elite profitable compounders can qualify with a smaller pullback when valuation compression, major support or a broad-market dislocation creates an attractive setup.
qualificationModel.tariffRule: Tariffs are not a qualification filter or score penalty. They may be noted only as temporary earnings/macro context.
qualificationModel.hardwareRule: Hardware, med-tech and asset-heavier businesses are allowed when margins, balance sheet, recurring ecosystem economics and long-term growth quality are strong.

researchFunnel.universeDefinition: This published snapshot was produced from a legacy curated 20-name research set. The next manual `generate` is required to use the new broad 150–300 stock discovery funnel. Counts that were not tracked by the legacy pass are left null rather than invented.

trendIntegrityPolicy.structuralReject: Reject when persistent trend deterioration stacks across moving-average structure, negative slopes, severe 6/12-month returns, large drawdown, repeated lower monthly closes and weak relative strength.
trendIntegrityPolicy.qualityTrap: Quarantine profitable chronic underperformers when long-term relative-price damage is combined with at least two business-deterioration flags.
trendIntegrityPolicy.reentry: Quarantined names require business repair plus at least three technical repair signals; prior structural-downtrend rejects require at least four.
